seller_questions: Can you send the PCNA dealer service history printout for VIN [VIN], plus any independent receipts that came with the car?
Has recall 21V679000 (rear-axle carrier) been completed, and on what date and at what mileage?
Will you print the DME over-rev report (ranges 1-6 with ignition cycles and engine hours) and a full PIWIS fault-memory scan?
What is the date and mileage of the most recent water pump, coolant and brake fluid service?
What brand and model are the tires, are they N-spec, and what are the four DOT date codes?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, including the first 60 seconds of idle?
Can you send a video of the top cycling fully open and closed three times, plus photos of the rear trunk area and front footwell carpets lifted?
Can you share actual photos of this car, including the underside, the front bumper corner ducts and radiators, and the engine bay access panels?
What is the exact factory paint and interior name, and can you provide the option code sheet or window sticker?
Was this car a trade-in from its original owner, and what did your service department find or do in reconditioning (with the RO)?
Will you allow an independent Porsche specialist PPI, including a borescope, before any deposit?
ppi_focus: DME over-rev report and PIWIS scan read by the inspecting specialist, not only the selling dealer.
Borescope all six cylinders and listen for cold-start ticking (9A1 scoring check).
Cooling system pressure test, coolant level history and water pump weep check; inspect the expansion tank and hard lines for crust.
Crankcase vacuum test (AOS health) and check the RMS and case seam for oil film on the bellhousing.
Clutch engagement point, DMF rattle at idle and judder from a stop.
Cycle the top 3-4 times; inspect drains, rear window seam, and footwell and seat-area carpet padding for dampness or corrosion.
Pull the front corner liners: condensers, radiators, debris.
Rear-axle carrier recall status and underside corrosion survey on this Maryland car; paint-meter all panels.
Tire date codes and N-spec status; brake pad and rotor life.
Confirm factory exhaust with cats present for CA smog.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a PCNA/receipt file showing regular oil, brake fluid, coolant and water pump service, plus a clean over-rev report and borescope.
Up: actual photos and an independent PPI confirming a dry engine, healthy clutch, functioning top and a dry interior.
Up: a negotiated price reduction or an included water pump/fluid service.
Down: over-rev hits in ranges 5-6, borescope scoring, unexplained coolant loss, or evidence of water intrusion.
Down: undisclosed paintwork or a refusal of an independent PPI before deposit.
evidence.mission_note: A 981 S manual in blue over tan is a credible future-keeper archetype, but at $44,799 it is attractive only as a keeper and conflicts with the current cash-preservation priority while the RX is the household's only car. It does not solve the near-term bridge need cheaply.
evidence.rationale: The VIN decode confirms a 2013 Porsche Boxster with the 3.4L flat-six, consistent with the listing's S trim. The listing establishes a manual transmission, 46,553 miles, blue over tan, and an AutoCheck summary of clean title, one owner and no reported accidents. The tracker's '987.2' tag is wrong; this is a 981. The attached images are manufacturer stock renders of a silver/red car, so no condition evidence about this specific car was examined here. Recall 21V679000 for the rear-axle carrier applies to this model year and its completion is unconfirmed. None of the 9A1-specific protections are present in the captured text: over-rev report, PIWIS scan, borescope, cooling-system history, top function. On a 13-year-old car, the water pump, brake fluid, plugs and battery are age-due unless records show otherwise. Price is roughly in line with the sparse comps for an S manual at this mileage, with no repair items established by the listing itself.
evidence.next_action: Ask Porsche Bethesda for the PCNA service history printout, recall 21V679000 completion record, DME over-rev report, PIWIS scan and real photos of this car, and confirm in writing that an independent Porsche-specialist PPI can be done before any deposit.
